points: The median ad went live Nov 19, 9 days out. After Nov 21, the biggest days were Thanksgiving (3,555 ads) and Black Friday itself (3,213).
Size didn't buy a head start: pages with 1M+ followers launched their first a median 11 days out; pages under 100K, 13 to 14.
Home and furniture started earliest (17 days out). Food and drink, and pets, started latest (9).
22% of early-access ads used a Sign Up button instead of Shop Now.
32,551 English ads named a percentage. The middle half ran 30% to 60%; 57% went to 50% or deeper, and 17% to 70% or deeper.
"Up to" was on half of percent-off ads, and lifted the median from 40% (flat discounts) to 50%.
Of 882 brands with percent-off ads both two weeks out and in Black Friday week, 64% kept the same number, 26% went deeper and 10% went shallower.
Brand size didn't move it: the median was 50% in every follower band, from under 10K to 1M+.
Inside the same brand the run-length gaps shrink to a day or three: dollars off ran 9 days against percent off's 6, across 64 brands. Free shipping and gifts showed no edge.
29% of videos ran 15 seconds or less, and 14% ran over a minute.
30% of ads announced the sale was live or here, and 12% said limited time.
Shop Now was on 71% of ads, Learn More 15%, Sign Up 3%. 26% sent people to a product page, 25% to a sale page, 12% to the homepage.
Where a brand ran both formats in the EU, its highest-reach ad was a video 54% of the time, against video's 47% share of its ads (1,031 brands).
Measured across 398 brands that ran both kinds of ad. In the full pull the gap is smaller, 47% against 42%, and points the same way.
Across all brands the long-runners also carried twice the social proof, but inside the same brand that gap disappears: it was the kind of brand, not the ad.
The median ad ran 6 days, and two-thirds had stopped by Cyber Monday.
The record: a "Pre Black Friday Sale: 35% off" ad that ran 369 days, from Oct 16, 2025 to Oct 20, 2026.
The median Cyber Monday ad launched on Cyber Monday itself; 83% went live on or after Black Friday.
Of 357 brands with percent-off ads for both days, 28% went deeper on Cyber Monday and 11% went shallower.
Only 3% of the ads launched Dec 2 to 7 said "extended".
0.5% of brands ran all four acts: early access, Black Friday, Cyber Monday and after. Two-thirds ran the Black Friday act alone.
todo: Plan backwards from Nov 14 this year: 13 days out, where the median brand's first ad landed last year. Get early access live around Nov 10, and anything you ship before that is ahead of most of the feed.
Pick the number early and say it the same way everywhere, as most brands did. If yours is 50%, the number alone won't stand out: put the product or the reason right beside it.
If anything you sell is giftable, the gift and bundle lanes were close to empty: a gift with purchase led about 1 in 100 Black Friday ads.
Write the headline nobody else can: the product, the offer and the reason in one line. "Black Friday Sale" ran on 1,425 ads on its own.
Build statics you can run all season, not just a launch-day video. And give every Black Friday ad an end date: 1,232 were still running in September.
Brief the Cyber Monday ad now, while it's cheap to make: 7 in 8 brands won't have one. Then turn the copy to gifting from Dec 2.
